content.comment_body: Hello. I have an interesting question. Is there any reason the program stored in the controller could be erased on its own? I write and test my program, but after a few weeks, it disappears from the controller and I need to reload it. What could cause this?

Hello [user_name]; Which version of software are you using and what is the part number of your [product_name] controller? When do you notice the program has been lost? Does it happen during power off/on, after downloading, or when stopping/starting? A screenshot of any error messages could be helpful. Hope this helps, [user_name]

Usually, the program can only be deleted intentionally. When transferring a program from the PC to the [product_name], it should be saved in the device's flash memory. Are there any unusual events, such as power failures? Is there an SD card with an empty program inserted in the [product_name]?

I think this happens during power interruptions. Would writing the program to an SD card help? My software is [product_name] Soft Comfort [version_no]. Controller is 24CE [product_name] [article_no]. Why does the program erase from memory when power is lost—is this normal?

No, that's not normal. The program should be stored in flash memory in a fail-safe way. This is why I asked if there's an SD card in the [product_name] with an empty program. That could explain what you're experiencing.
Interesting. Yes, there was an empty SD card inserted, and removing it actually resolved the issue. Now, when the power cycles, the program remains intact. Thanks very much!

analysis.insight_summary: The user faced a scenario where their controller’s program disappeared after power cycling, needing a manual re-upload. This situation created confusion about memory retention reliability and potential unintended data loss. The underlying user experience problem highlighted a lack of clear feedback or warning regarding program retention when using an empty SD card.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the controller to reliably retain their program in memory following power loss—without unexpected deletion or silent changes caused by SD card usage.
